{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Sharpe's Peril is a British TV film from 2008, usually shown in two parts, which is part of an ITV series based on Bernard Cornwell's historical fiction novels about the English soldier Richard Sharpe during the Napoleonic Wars.","title":"Sharpe's Peril"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Contrary to most parts of the TV series, \"Sharpe's Peril\" isn't based on one of Cornwell's novels.","title":"Sharpe's Peril"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Both are set in 1817, two years after Sharpe has retired as a farmer in Normandy, so chronologically they come after \"Sharpe's Waterloo\" (1815) and before the final novel \"Sharpe's Devil\" (1820–21).","title":"Sharpe's Peril"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" In \"Sharpe's Challenge\" and \"Sharpe's Peril\", Sharpe and his comrade in arms, Patrick Harper, have been temporarily called out of retirement and asked to go to India.","title":"Sharpe's Peril"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Faulconer County is a fictional county in the state of Virginia, a setting in the Starbuck Chronicles by Bernard Cornwell set during the American Civil War.","title":"Faulconer County"}],"peer_messages":["Unverified peer answer: American Civil War\nEvidence: {\"sentence_id\":0,\"text\":\"The Starbuck Chronicles are a series of historical fiction novels by British author Bernard Cornwell set during the American Civil War.\",\"title\":\"The Starbuck Chronicles\"}"],"previous_answer":"American Civil War","question":"What type of conflict does Nathaniel Starbuck and Bernard Cornwell have in common?"}
